sources.title: Michel Brion, Introduction to actions of algebraic groups (2010), Les cours du CIRM 1(1) 1–22
sources.locator: §1.1, Definition 1.4, Lemma 1.5, Definition 1.6, Example 1.7, Definition 1.8 and the complete proof of Proposition 1.9; printed pp. 3–4 (PDF pp. 4–5) of the retrieved 23-page article. Full text retrieved and the listed sections read; no later section is claimed.

contents.name: Definition 1.4 (G-variety; algebraic G-action; induced linear action on C[X])
Lemma 1.5 (C[X] is a union of finite-dimensional G-stable subspaces on which G acts algebraically)
Definition 1.6 (rational G-module; finite-dimensional modules as homomorphisms to GL_n)
Remark after Definition 1.6 (left multiplication on the rational-function space C(G) is not a rational G-module)
contents.reason: The non-rational left-translation action on the rational-function space C(G) is not built; the pair's counterexample instead constructs its own abstract translation action on A^1 and checks the nonregular matrix coefficient directly.

contents.name: Example 1.7 (G=C^*: Z-grading of C[X], conversely finitely generated graded algebras without nonzero nilpotents, and T_n/Z^n-graded algebras)
Proposition 1.9 with complete proof (equivariant isomorphism of an affine G-variety onto a closed G-subvariety of a finite-dimensional G-module)

sources.title: Philippe Gille, Introduction to reductive group schemes over rings (author notes, marked in construction)
sources.locator: §6, Proposition 6.0.5 with its two diagrams and proof, pp. 25–27; Proposition 6.2.1 with the full-faithfulness and essential-surjectivity proof, pp. 30–31; Theorem 6.3.1 with proof, p. 32. Retrieved 113-page author file; printed and PDF pages agree over the claimed range.

contents.name: Proposition 6.0.5 (comodule diagrams (6.0.6)–(6.0.7) characterize representations, and conversely every comodule comes from a unique representation)
Proposition 6.2.1 (equivalence between A-graded R-modules and R-D(A)-modules; full faithfulness and essential surjectivity)
Theorem 6.3.1 (a k-G-representation V is the filtered union of its finite-dimensional subrepresentations)
Theorem 6.3.2 (an algebraic group over a field admits a finite-dimensional faithful representation)
contents.reason: Faithful linearity of the group is a different claim from the pair's equivariant embedding of the acted-on affine set: a group acting trivially on a generating module would not be faithfully represented, so no item here consumes or asserts it.
